# Primitive Representation

Also called: Gaussian Primitives, Splatting Kernels

## Overview
Primitive Representation defines the geometric and photometric data structures used to approximate a 3D scene in Gaussian Splatting methods [G]. It solves the problem of representing continuous geometry and appearance with discrete, differentiable primitives that can be efficiently rasterized [G]. It sets itself apart from parent methods by explicitly defining the kernel shape (e.g., isotropic, half-space, or hybrid Bézier) and the associated attribute storage (e.g., opacity, normals, control points) that determine how light interacts with the primitive during rendering [G].

## Shared principles
All child methods share the core requirement of defining a 3D primitive with a position, orientation, scale, and appearance attributes [G]. The standard 3D Gaussian primitive is defined by a mean $\boldsymbol{\mu}$ for position, a covariance $\Sigma$ for shape and orientation, and appearance attributes like Spherical Harmonics coefficients and opacity $\alpha$ [G]. Parameterized as $\Sigma^w = R S S^T R^T$ in world space, where $R$ is rotation and $S$ is scaling [G]. The rendering pipeline projects these 3D primitives to 2D screen space [G]. The covariance transforms via the view matrix $W$ and projection Jacobian $J$: $\Sigma = J W \Sigma^w W^T J^T$ [G]. The integral of the 3D density along the view direction yields the 2D splat density [G].

## Subtopics

### [3D Half-Gaussian Splatting](9011-3d-half-gaussian-splatting.md)
[3D Half-Gaussian Splatting](9011-3d-half-gaussian-splatting.md) replaces the standard full 3D Gaussian with a 3D Half-Gaussian to address shape and color discontinuities at object boundaries. It achieves higher rendering quality without compromising speed by allowing each half of the split Gaussian to have different opacity values while sharing geometric parameters. Unlike 2D-GS, which performs surface rendering, 3D-HGS retains volumetric rendering to preserve performance while enabling accurate modeling of discontinuous functions.

### [Bézier Gaussian Triangle](11816-b-zier-gaussian-triangle.md)
[Bézier Gaussian Triangle](11816-b-zier-gaussian-triangle.md) is a hybrid 3D primitive representation that combines Bézier triangle surfaces for explicit geometry with 3D Gaussian sub-primitives for appearance, enabling differentiable rendering with sharp boundaries. It solves the problem of blurry or aliased edges common in pure Gaussian splatting by defining the object's silhouette and surface topology via parametric Bézier patches, while using Gaussians only for shading and color. Unlike standard 3D Gaussian Splatting, which relies on the overlap of many opaque Gaussians to form shapes, BG-Triangle maintains distinct, sharp boundaries between primitives, making it particularly suitable for vectorization and compact scene representation.

### Gaussian Surfels
Uses zero-thickness oriented surfels [S1, unofficial]. This variant represents primitives as planar disks with normal vectors, often used for surface extraction or meshing, differing from volumetric Gaussians by enforcing zero thickness [S1, unofficial].
